sections.heading: C - Special Driving Situations
sections.markdown:
## C - Special Driving Situations

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Night driving outranks daylight in difficulty and danger, with sight chained to headlight throw [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
Burn high beams whenever none approach since they double low-beam reach, dip for oncoming metal, drop to lows behind followers and in fog, rain, or snow where highs glare, optionally fog-lamping storms, and always dim within 500 feet of oncoming cars and 300 feet of leaders [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Glare-blind, aim eyes at the right edge while scanning past your beams for dark lumps, edge-check both shoulders, ditch sunglasses and tints at night and under clouds, pad following by at least one extra second at night and two on strange night roads, and switch lamps on whenever others look dim [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Funeral columns own intersections behind yellow, red, or blue escort flashers, yielding only to emergency iron, police orders, and trains, so never split the column, fake right-of-way with lamps or stunts, or pass riders without orders or beyond city, town, and urban-county limits [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A02
Interstates and parkways also free procession passing, while violators face a $250 fine or 90 days in jail [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A02
Work zones fence roadwork with closures, detours, and machines, wounding some 40,000 people yearly, so approach hunting orange-on-black signs, cones, barrels, trucks, and crews, always slowing for tight lanes and rough skin even when deserted, since Kentucky doubles signed-zone fines wherever at least one true worker stands [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A02
Inside zones, slow down, stretch gaps, track neighbors, coil to stop, drive doubly wary after dark, slide over for crews and iron, obey every board through End Road Work, budget delays with early starts, and detour around whenever possible [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A02
Rural blacktop kills the unwary, so heed signs and limits; gravel and dirt sap grip, demanding slower speeds, longer gaps, and skid-ready stops, while narrow ditch-lined strips want centered slow cars watching for lane-borrowing opposites [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A02
Heed narrow and single-lane bridge warnings and trade crossings, with first arrival holding the right-of-way [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A03
Steel and open-grate decks skate, so slow, gap, and grip hard; wooded, cropped, and hilly blind corners demand slow stop-ready rolling; and uncontrolled rural crossings want the same for crossing and oncoming metal [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A03
Autocycles seat riders car-style over three grounded wheels past 40 miles per hour, side-by-side or tandem under open or capped tops, belted three-point with optional bags or cages, steered by wheel and pedals, yet never alternative-speed motorcycles [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A03
Autocycles count as motorcycles for traffic law but need no cycle license or endorsement beyond a valid operator's license, and riders skip headgear mandates [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A03
Towing spans billions of yearly miles with judgment as the linchpin, since driver error mothers most rig crashes, so hitch, load, and run correctly with sixty percent of cargo weight forward and 40 percent aft to strangle sway [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A04
Swaying, steer dead straight and bleed speed without brakes and never faster, park fully clear soonest, re-pin front-heavy loading with heavies floored, tight packing, and tied partials [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A04
Tow with a compensating mind at a lazier pace, capping near 55 mph, never topping posted limits, slowing further as weather sours, and braking before grades begin [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A04
Rigs stop and pass longer, so bank extra nose room swelling in rain, snow, and fog, budget hill and curve passes, and swing turns wide since trailers cheat inside [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A04
Back trailers slowly with a bottom-wheel hand steering the tail where the hand points, and at jackknife freeze, pull ahead straight, then retry [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A04
Pros counsel expert help when unsure, combination thinking, walk-around hitch, chain, light, and tire checks before rolling and at every fuel stop, safe pull-offs for strange noises, and rested daylight legs over straight-through marathons [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A04
The safe-tow checklist chants heavy front, tight hitch, chained, lit, aired, slowed, thinking ahead, rested, inspected, secured, and belted [A04].
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ky-d:kentucky-state-police-ksp-driver-testing:handbook:pdf-0079]
